cases.name: highlight-defaults
cases.covers: A highlight with nothing but its quads. Every default the writer supplies is visible here: the family colour, the opacity it writes rather than omits, and the /Rect derived from the quads.

cases.name: highlight-two-quads
cases.covers: Two quads, so /Rect has to enclose both. A writer that used only the first would produce a box that is right for one line of a two-line selection.

cases.name: highlight-everything
cases.covers: Colour, opacity, contents, subject, an /NM the caller chose, and flags. The whole base surface at once.

cases.name: underline-default-colour
cases.covers: The other text-markup default. Highlight falls back to yellow and the rest to black, so a writer with one fallback for all four agrees with three.

cases.name: squiggly
cases.covers: The third of the family, to prove the subtype code reaches the document.

cases.name: strikeout-plain
cases.covers: A standalone strikeout, which has no /IT at all.

cases.name: strikeout-text-edit
cases.covers: The subordinate half of a replace-text edit. /IT is written as StrikeOutTextEdit, with the capital O that neither the subtype nor the wire word has.

cases.name: square-defaults
cases.covers: A square with nothing but its rect. The resolved border a reader reports for an annotation with no /BS is what the writer has to produce.

cases.name: square-decorated
cases.covers: Every optional shape entry: a dashed border with a pattern, a fill, a cloudy intensity and an /RD inset.

cases.name: square-degenerate-cloudy
cases.covers: A cloudy intensity of zero. The wire domain is positive-or-null, so the writer has to clear rather than write a value the reader would then normalize away.

cases.name: square-rotated
cases.covers: A rotated box. `/Rect` is the enclosing axis-aligned box of the turned square; the pair under /EMBD_Metadata is what makes the generator bake a turned appearance rather than an upright one.

cases.name: square-zero-rotation
cases.covers: A box whose logical box is its rect and whose rotation is zero. Zero degrees clears the key rather than writing it, so the annotation carries a box and no angle.

cases.name: square-zero-rotation-no-box
cases.covers: Zero degrees with no logical box, which is not the unsatisfiable pair. Nothing is being rotated, so there is nothing for a box to be the pre-rotation form of.

cases.name: polygon
cases.covers: A closed vertex path with a fill and a cloudy border. Only a polygon takes /BE: an open path has no interior for one to enclose.

cases.name: polyline-with-endings
cases.covers: An open vertex path with a /LE pair, which the polygon family does not have. The two endings differ, so a writer that wrote one twice is visible.

cases.name: polyline-defaults
cases.covers: The same without a /LE, so the pair that draws nothing is what a reader gets back rather than an absent entry it has to interpret.

cases.name: line
cases.covers: Two endpoints and a pair of endings, which is the whole of a line annotation.

cases.name: ink-two-strokes
cases.covers: Two pen strokes, so a writer that appended only the first is visible, with the highlighter intent that is the only /IT ink carries.

cases.name: polygon-zero-cloud
cases.covers: A cloudy intensity of zero, which is not a cloud. A writer that passed it through writes a /BE that says the border is cloudy with no waviness, which is a different dictionary from the one a plain border has.

cases.name: polyline-zero-rotation
cases.covers: A rotation of zero. Zero degrees is not a rotation, so the key is cleared rather than stamped, and a file that had none keeps none.

cases.name: ink-advisory-rotation
cases.covers: A rotation scalar on a vertex kind. Since 6153c181e the strokes are stored upright and the generator turns them by this angle about the middle of their box; it never carries a logical box, which is what separates it from the shape family.

cases.name: text-defaults
cases.covers: A sticky note with nothing named. The icon and the yellow fill are written explicitly rather than left to the file, so a read reports the same thing a draft that named them would.

cases.name: text-reviewed
cases.covers: An icon other than the default, and the review pair. `/State` and `/StateModel` are dictionary-only, so a note that has been accepted is drawn exactly like one that has not.

cases.name: text-model-alone
cases.covers: A state model with no state, which §12.5.6.3 allows: the model implies its own default. The reverse is refused, and that refusal is a draft-only rule.

cases.name: text-foreign-state
cases.covers: A model nobody standardized. Acrobat lets a workflow register one, and the reader passes it through, so the writer has to be able to write it back rather than normalize it into a standard name.

cases.name: caret-defaults
cases.covers: A caret with only a rect. The red mark is the engine-wide default.

cases.name: caret-replace
cases.covers: The caret half of a replace-text edit, with the inset of the drawn symbol from its box.

cases.name: caret-rotated
cases.covers: A caret is a BOX kind, so its rotation is the pair and not the lone scalar the vertex families carry.

cases.name: free-text-plain
cases.covers: A plain text box. The three colours are three different entries: /DA draws the border and the text, /C is the background, and a TextColor override is absent here so the text follows /DA.

cases.name: free-text-three-colours
cases.covers: All three at once, with a text colour that overrides the /DA one. A writer that wrote /DA after the override would put the border colour back over the text.

draft.contents: Red text, blue border, cream box.

created.contents: Red text, blue border, cream box.

runs.text: Red text, blue border, cream box.

cases.name: free-text-callout
cases.covers: A callout: the same annotation with a /CL leader and an ending on the called-out end. The other end touches the text box, where an arrowhead would be drawn into the box it belongs to.

cases.name: free-text-rotated
cases.covers: A box kind, so the rotation is the pair. A callout would rotate its text box alone and leave the leader in page space.

cases.name: redact-area
cases.covers: An area redaction: no quads, so /Rect is the region. Nothing here removes anything; the marking declares what apply would do.

cases.name: redact-text-with-label
cases.covers: A text redaction with quads, the /IC fill painted after apply, and a tiled label. The /DA is emitted because a label obliges one.

cases.name: redact-autofit-label
cases.covers: A label at size zero, which for a redaction means auto-fit to the region rather than nothing. Free text refuses the same number.

cases.name: redact-empty-label
cases.covers: An empty overlay text, which is not a label. A writer that wrote it would put an /OverlayText on the annotation that draws nothing and obliges a /DA beside it.

cases.name: file-attachment
cases.covers: A marker and the file it names. PDFium derives the size, the checksum and the creation date from the bytes, so the read back proves the stream was written and not just the filespec.

cases.name: file-attachment-defaults
cases.covers: The writer default icon is the paperclip, which is NOT what an absent /Name reads as. The key is always written, so the two never disagree about one file.

cases.name: link-dead
cases.covers: A link with nowhere to go. This is the create-then-edit flow: the rectangle is dragged first and the destination chosen afterwards, so a target of null is a legitimate state rather than a mistake.

cases.name: link-uri
cases.covers: A /URI action. The reader normalizes /Dest and /A /GoTo together, so this is the one target shape it cannot confuse with the other.

cases.name: link-goto-xyz
cases.covers: An /XYZ destination with a left and a top and no zoom. Each component is present or retains the current value, so the absent zoom has to come back absent rather than as a zero magnification.

cases.name: link-goto-fit
cases.covers: The parameterless fit, which writes an empty array rather than a padded one.

cases.name: link-goto-fit-h
cases.covers: One positional parameter. A fit type takes its parameters by position, so an absent one can only be absent by shortening the array.

cases.name: link-goto-xyz-retain
cases.covers: An /XYZ whose left retains the current value. Zero is a real coordinate at the left edge, so an absent left cannot be written as one.

cases.name: link-goto-fit-h-retain
cases.covers: A /FitH with no top. The parameter is positional, so absent means a shorter array rather than a zero at the bottom of the page.

cases.name: link-goto-fit-v
cases.covers: The vertical twin of /FitH. It takes a left where the other takes a top, and they are different view codes, so a writer with one code for both agrees with one of them.

cases.name: link-goto-fit-bv
cases.covers: The bounding-box variants are a separate pair of codes again, fitting the content box rather than the crop box.

cases.name: link-goto-fit-r
cases.covers: The one fit type whose four coordinates are all required.

cases.name: stamp-png-contain
cases.covers: A 4x2 image in a square box under the default fit. Aspect is preserved and the leftover space is split evenly, so a writer that pinned the image to a corner is visible in the appearance.

cases.name: stamp-png-cover
cases.covers: The same bytes filling the box instead, which crops rather than letterboxes.

cases.name: stamp-png-fill
cases.covers: And distorting it, which is the one policy that discards the aspect ratio.

cases.name: stamp-other-name
cases.covers: A second enumerated label, to prove the code reaches the document rather than one label being hardcoded. A label outside the set is refused: the reader reports a custom /Name a file carries, and the writer will not author one.

cases.name: stamp-rotated
cases.covers: A rotated stamp, authored in the unrotated frame and turned by an /AP matrix. Fitting into the rotated box instead bakes the letterbox bands in and the closing re-fit shrinks the image a second time.

cases.name: highlight-cleared-strings
cases.covers: A draft that explicitly clears contents and subject. Setting a null value writes an EMPTY string rather than removing the key, so a writer that used the setter would produce a field that reads back as present-and-empty instead of absent.

cases.name: highlight-empty-nm
cases.covers: An /NM the caller supplied as an empty string. An empty name is not an identity, so it is not written: two annotations could both carry it and neither would be addressable.

cases.name: square-null-interior
cases.covers: A shape whose fill is explicitly null, beside the default case where it is simply absent. Both mean a shape with no fill.

cases.name: circle-defaults
cases.covers: The other shape subtype, which shares every field and differs only in its code.
